q1: SELECT ITM.ITEMNO, ITEMPRICE.NP FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ITM.ITEMNO, ITEMPRICE.NP FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
counterexample: INSERT INTO ITM (ITEMNO, TYPE) VALUES (1, 1); INSERT INTO ITP (ITEMNO, NP) VALUES (1, 10), (1, 20);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 first selects distinct ITEMNO and NP from ITP, then joins with ITM on ITEMNO. Q2 joins ITP and ITM directly and selects distinct ITEMNO and NP. The difference arises when ITP has duplicate ITEMNO values, as Q1 removes duplicates from ITP first before joining, while Q2 removes duplicates after joining.
counterexample_dsp: A test case with duplicate ITEMNO entries in ITP but distinct ITEMNO in ITM. Q1 will return fewer rows due to the DISTINCT applied before the join, while Q2 will return more rows before applying DISTINCT after the join.
